method: Read primary EC3 table text/footers, directly inspect the applicable #256 annotation, current ledger and consumers, and actual test bodies. No tests executed and no network/external URI handler was invoked.

source_locations.coverage: Table 196 entries Type/S/Next are on 521/506; Note 1 sequence semantics and recommendations continue on 522/507.

Table 210's URI and IsMap cells, click-only rule, coordinate conversion/rounding formula, Table 211 Base and Note all appear before the 519 footer. Physical 535 begins 12.6.4.9 and is not a Table 211 continuation.

features.title: Entries common to all action dictionaries

cells.requirement: Optional name; if present, shall be Action.
cells.coverage: The action reader dispatches by /S and does not use /Type as a performability gate. No assertion in this bounded pass establishes a contrary reader-rejection duty.

cells.requirement: Required action-type name; action-specific entries are defined by Table 201 and following tables.
cells.coverage: The action reader dispatches supported names and keeps named refusals for unsupported known types. Broader action-kind coverage belongs to other shards.

cells.requirement: Optional dictionary or ordered array; every action's own Next follows recursively. Note 1 recommends reasonable treatment of anomalous cases, including not repeating self-referential actions and terminating when an action makes a later one impossible. It also says applications need a mechanism for user interruption.
cells.coverage: Current parser preserves ordered occurrences and path-cycle treatment; parent-review.json for actions_chains_current records executed repeated-sibling and cycle controls (actions-wave19b.log). Code caps flattened performed actions at 256 and visits at 1024; no per-sequence user-interrupt control was identified in the core call path. The source does not say the cap is an interrupt mechanism. This is recorded as a narrow owner/source question, not as a demonstrated behavioral failure. Multiple document-replacement actions remain separately unresolved in the earlier action-chain shard.

features.title: Additional entries specific to a URI action

cells.coverage: Current action parser has an explicit URI branch.

cells.requirement: Required ASCII string encoded in UTF-8; the URI is resolved.
cells.coverage: pdf-model resolves against Catalog URI/Base when present; viewer-host resolves a remaining partial reference against the opened document location where available. Resolution is separate from any decision to open/fetch.

cells.requirement: Optional boolean, default false. Only applies to a URI action triggered by a user clicking an annotation; explicitly ignored for outline-item and catalog OpenAction actions. A click point is transformed device-to-user, offset from the associated annotation Rect's upper-left, rounded to nearest integers, and appended after ? separated by comma.
cells.coverage: Tracked uri_ismap_click_spec_audit.rs covers literal click geometry, default/false, fractional rounding and OpenAction ignore; public headless.rs outline URI test only asserts a URI handoff and does not set IsMap. The scratch draft pairs one public outline action and one link click using the same IsMap=true action, without opening the URI.

cells.requirement: Optional ASCII string. A partial URI action reference is resolved relative to this URI when present; without it the reference is interpreted relative to the document location. Note says this supports moved/out-of-context documents and links to resources that stayed at their original location.
cells.coverage: Model action tests cover explicit Base, no Base, and absolute URI precedence. Host mapping tests cover opened-document location fallback and unresolved relative path behavior. EC3 #256 broadens the Base text to all relative URIs in a PDF, not only URI actions. No fetch/open is part of this shard.

errata.source: Primary EC3 physical p.534, annotation with Subj Issue #256; Review/Completed reply attached to that annotation.
errata.effect: The Editor Note says the remaining §12.6.4.8 Base/URI-dictionary text applies to all relative URIs in a PDF, not just URI actions as the placement suggests; a future edition may move it. This is a scope clarification, not a strike/caret edit to Tables 210-211.
errata.existing_record: doc/errata-read.md records #256 under §12.6.4.8; pdf-model action and file-spec URL callers cite the broadened scope.

limits: Does not certify every action type or all URI schemes, link geometry transforms, or native host event paths.
Does not make ISO action semantics permission to launch, browse, fetch, or send a request; all observations stop at the caller-visible Event::OpenUri boundary.
Passing existing click/OpenAction tests do not establish the outline IsMap exception; the scratch draft is proposed evidence and has not been run.

A URI action nested below /Next raises an interpretive question about whether the initiating click is the trigger for that nested action; this pass does not turn shared click context into a separate defect.
parent_execution: T162 public outline/link test PASS. The same IsMap=true action emits the bare URI on outline activation and literal ?10,6 on an annotation click. No handler invoked. Pending draft statements below are superseded.
